title: TSMC 2026 OIP Ecosystem Forum Summary
gist: Daniel Nenni summarizes TSMC's 2026 OIP Ecosystem Forum: AI performance now requires system-level co-optimization across logic, memory, packaging, photonics and power, with TSMC's 5.5-reticle CoWoS in production and a path to >14 reticles. Also notable: 200Gbps COUPE micro-ring modulator in production targeting 4Tbps/mm by 2030, a shift toward inference-optimized memory options, and an agentic 'AI Design Kit'.

insights.claim: TSMC argues that faster AI chips require progress across the whole system, including logic, memory, packaging, interconnects, power delivery and design methods, not just transistor scaling.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Value capture broadens to packaging, memory, photonics and power-delivery suppliers in TSMC's ecosystem.
insights.quote: faster chips will require progress across the whole system: logic, memory, packaging, interconnects, power delivery and design methods

insights.claim: TSMC frames AI scaling as constrained by memory capacity, data movement and power consumption even as compute needs rise rapidly.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Memory bandwidth, interconnect and power efficiency are the bottlenecks to own.
insights.quote: memory capacity, data movement and power consumption constrain what systems can deliver
insights.locator: AI is also changing the kinds

insights.claim: TSMC cites robotaxis, humanoid robotics and AR/VR as AI applications driving demand for advanced-node silicon.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Edge/physical AI as next leg of advanced-node demand beyond datacentre.
insights.quote: TSMC pointed to applications including robotaxis, humanoid robotics and augmented or virtual reality
insights.locator: AI is also changing the kinds

insights.claim: TSMC expands the design boundary to the system level, naming COUPE, integrated voltage regulation, capacitors and thermal design-technology co-optimization as relevant from AI chips through data centers, and calling for closer collaboration with ODMs.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: TSMC pushing into datacentre-level design deepens its lock-in and touches ODM/power-component supply chains.
insights.quote: TSMC expands the design boundary to the system level.
insights.locator: Bottom line: TSMC expands the design

insights.claim: TSMC's OIP includes 28 trusted partners, more than 100,000 silicon-verified, production-proven IP offerings and over 3,000 engineers spanning concept through silicon.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Ecosystem depth is a moat that competing foundries (Intel, Samsung) struggle to replicate.
insights.quote: TSMC cites 28 trusted partners, more than 100,000 silicon-verified and production-proven IP offerings, and over 3,000 engineers
insights.locator: The keynotes began with the scale

insights.claim: TSMC's message is that customers need dependable IP and validated design flows as much as an advanced manufacturing process.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Explains why foundry share is sticky beyond pure process technology.
insights.quote: customers need dependable components and validated design flows as much as they need an advanced manufacturing process
insights.locator: The keynotes began with the scale

insights.claim: TSMC says its 5.5-times-reticle CoWoS package is in production and describes a path toward packages larger than 14 reticles, supported by the 3DFabric Alliance.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Package size growth implies rising interposer, substrate, HBM and test content per AI accelerator.
insights.quote: its 5.5-times-reticle CoWoS package is in production and describes a path toward packages larger than 14 reticles
insights.locator: Advanced packaging is another major focus.

insights.claim: As AI shifts from training toward inference and agentic applications, TSMC expects demand for memory options optimized for bandwidth, latency and power, including 3D-stacked SRAM, HBM and DRAM integrated with logic.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Inference shift could diversify memory architectures beyond HBM, benefiting SRAM-stacking and logic-integrated DRAM approaches.
insights.quote: As more AI work shifts from training toward inference and agentic applications, TSMC expects demand for memory choices optimized for bandwidth, latency and power.
insights.locator: Advanced packaging is another major focus.

insights.claim: New memory-integration options require cooperation among EDA providers, IP suppliers, memory companies, assembly and test firms, and substrate makers.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Broadens beneficiaries of AI packaging to substrates, OSATs and EDA.
insights.quote: These options call for cooperation among electronic-design-automation providers, IP suppliers, memory companies, assembly and test firms, and substrate makers.
insights.locator: Advanced packaging is another major focus.

insights.claim: TSMC says a 200 Gbps micro-ring modulator using its COUPE technology is in production with a bit-error rate below 10^-8.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Co-packaged optics moving into production at TSMC; relevant for optical interconnect suppliers and competitors.
insights.quote: a 200-gigabit-per-second micro-ring modulator using its COUPE technology is in production

insights.claim: TSMC's photonics roadmap targets 400 Gbps modulation, multiple wavelengths and fiber-array integration, aiming for 4 terabits per second per millimeter by 2030.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Signals a multi-year co-packaged optics ramp; bandwidth density target sets competitive bar for CPO.
insights.quote: with a target of four terabits per second per millimeter by 2030

insights.claim: TSMC emphasizes power-efficiency gains in logic through process enhancements, DTCO and circuit design, with cell choice tailored to workload because energy use limits AI deployment.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Power efficiency, not just density, is the selling point of new nodes for AI.
insights.quote: particularly when energy use limits AI deployment

insights.claim: TSMC says more than 70% of OIP forum papers either use AI solutions or address AI use cases.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: AI-for-EDA is mainstream in the ecosystem; supports EDA vendors' AI narratives.
insights.quote: more than 70% of OIP forum papers either use AI solutions or address AI use cases

insights.claim: TSMC's proposed AI Design Kit (ADK) shifts design enablement toward an agentic AI framework incorporating design information and training material to raise productivity and shorten chip development time.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Agentic design kits could change the EDA/PDK value chain and TSMC's control over design flows.
insights.quote: shifts the design-enablement model toward an agentic AI framework

insights.claim: TSMC introduced six startups in an 'Emerging Technologies Alley' at the 2026 OIP forum.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Early signal of which startups TSMC is sponsoring.
insights.quote: introduces six startups in an “Emerging Technologies Alley.”
